summary: Johann Bernoulli was a scholar of history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Basel from around 1757 to 1764 and served as a Mitglied at the Prussian Academy of Sciences from circa 1764 to 1807.
Johann Christoph Adelung was a linguist who was educated at the Kloster Berge school from around 1746 to 1752 and studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1752 to 1754.

Scholar of religious studies and history/archaeology Johann Gottfried Eichhorn studied at the University of Göttingen under Christian Gottlob Heyne (~1770–1774). He held professorships of Oriental languages at Jena (~1775–1788) and philosophy at Göttingen (~1788–1827).

Johann Gottfried Ludwig Kosegarten worked in Indology and linguistics. After studying at the University of Greifswald (~1808–1812), he held posts at the University of Jena (~1817–1824) and as Professor at Greifswald (~1824–1850).

Johann Wilhelm Andreas Pfaff studied at the University of Tübingen (~1793–1797) and worked in Indology and other fields. He held posts at the Imperial University of Dorpat (~1803–1809), Würzburg (~1815–1818), and Erlangen-Nuremberg (~1818–1835).

Johanna Engelberta van Lohuizen-de Leeuw was an archaeologist and Indologist. After studying at Utrecht University (~1939–1949), she held posts at the University of Groningen (~1951–1959) and the University of Amsterdam, directing its Institute of South Asian Archaeology (~1959–1983).

Johanna Narten worked in linguistics, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology. She studied at Saarland University from circa 1951 to 1961 and held a post at the University of Erlangen-Nuremberg from around 1971 to 1993.

Johannes Beltz is a scholar of Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD by 1999 from both the University of Lausanne and the École Pratique des Hautes Études, studying under doctoral supervisors Johannes Bronkhorst and Marie-Louise Reiniche.

Johannes Bronkhorst, an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and philosopher, studied at VU Amsterdam, Savitribai Phule Pune University under S. D. Joshi (PhD ~1976–1979), and Leiden University (~1979–1980). In 1987, he was appointed Prof. dr. at the University of Lausanne.

Johannes Gildemeister studied under Heinrich Ewald at Göttingen (~1832–1834) and under Georg Wilhelm Freytag and Christian Lassen at Bonn (~1834–1838). In linguistics and Indology, he held professorships at the University of Marburg (~1845–1859) and University of Bonn (~1859–1890).

Indologist Johannes Hertel earned his PhD at Leipzig University (~1893–1897). He taught at Lessing-Gymnasium Döbeln (~1898–1920, attested as professor in 1927) and held the chair of Indian philology at Leipzig University from circa 1920 to 1937.

Indologist Johannes Klatt studied at the University of Halle-Wittenberg from circa 1869 to 1873, including under Albrecht Weber (~1872–1873). From around 1874 to 1892, he served as custos of the Indian department at the Berlin State Library.

Johannes Nobel, an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar, studied at Berlin (~1908–1911) under Heinrich Lüders (~1909–1913). He held posts at Berlin (~1920–1928) and the University of Marburg (~1928–1955; attested 1957 as Professor of Sanskrit).

Johannes Rahder studied at Utrecht University (~1915–1926). Specializing in Indology, Japanology, and Buddhist studies, he held posts at Utrecht (1930–1931), Leiden (1931–1946, Chair of Japanese), the University of Hawaii (1946–1947), and Yale University as professor (1961–1962).

Johannes Schmidt studied at Bonn (~1862–1865) and Jena (~1865–1866) under August Schleicher and Albrecht Weber. In linguistics and Indology, he held posts at Graz (~1872–1873), Bonn (~1873–1876), and as professor at Berlin (~1876–1901).

Johannes Schneider works in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies. He held a post at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities around 1996 and was an editorial board member at the Deshana Institute of Buddhist and Allied Studies as attested in 2021.

Scholar of Tibetology and sinology Johannes Schubert studied under August Conrady (~1920–1925) and August Hermann Francke (~1924–1928). He worked at Ahnenerbe (~1939–1945) and served as professor of Tibetan at Leipzig University (~1952–1966).

John A. Ardussi, a researcher in Tibetology, history, and archaeology, studied under MA supervisor Turrell V. Wylie and earned a PhD from the Australian National University (attested 1977). He has served on a research team at the CNRS.

John A. Brinkman is a historian and archaeologist. He served on the faculty at the University of Chicago from circa 1963 to 2005 and was a Professor at its Institute for the Study of Ancient Cultures from around 1964 to 2005.

Indologist and historian/archaeologist John Allan studied at the University of Edinburgh (~1903–1907) and Leipzig University (~1907–1908). He served at the British Museum, notably as Keeper of the Department of Coins and Medals from circa 1931 to 1949.
